title: Ops sunrise priority pipeline
content:
Quick morning brain-dump / runbook for today

Context: hopping into the 7:30–11:00 infra window. Primary focus: stabilise capacity for the batch embedding jobs, watch for egress spikes on edge pools, and finish the NVLink diagnostic flow we started yesterday.

Top priorities (order matters):
1) Batch embedding backlog (high)
   - Check queue: /opt/ops/tools/queue-stats --pool=batch-embeds
   - Target: get queue < 1200 tasks by noon. Current threshold where autoscale falters ~1500.
   - Action: if sustained > 1400 and p95 latency > 900ms, flip temporary routing to d-spot-3 (reserved) for 30m.
   - Quick command to reroute (dry-run first): ./route-override --from=batch-embeds --to=d-spot-3 --duration=30m --dry-run

2) GPU preemptions / MIG shuffle (medium-high)
   - Yesterday saw 3 preemptions on gnode-17 during a training job; logs indicate MIG allocation thrash.
   - Check node health: ssh ops@gnode-17; sudo nvidia-smi -q | grep -A3 "MIG"
   - If MIG allocations bouncing, restart kube-device-plugin on node and watch allocation events: kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset device-plugin && kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=gnode-17 -w
   - Note to self: propose a small throttling window for training jobs between 09:00–11:00 to reduce interference with batch inference.

3) Edge egress shaping (monitor)
   - Nightly spike from region eu-west-1 around 06:30 caused rate-limiter alerts. Might be a misconfigured collector.
   - Quick check: curl -sS https://obs-ingest.internal/redwood/metrics | jq '.egress | .["eu-west-1"] | .lastHour'
   - If > 80% of quota, add temporary rate-limit override for collector-7: ./egress-rate --set collector-7 50% --until 12:00

4) NVLink diagnostic follow-up (low-medium)
   - Tickets: PLAT-3427 (linked). Need to collect dmesg + nvlink stats, push to debug bucket.
   - Commands: sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-gnode-17.log; sudo nvidia-smi nvlink --show-topology > /tmp/nvlink-topo.log; rsync /tmp/*-gnode-17.log debug@debug-bucket:/incoming/gnode-17/

Operational notes / quick wins:
- Reminder: double-check the dedicated pool d-spot-3 has the new kernel (5.19.14) before routing heavy load. Last week it still had the older build and caused slowdowns.
- If making routing changes, post a short note in #infra-ops w/ the header: [TEMP ROUTE] <reason> <expected duration> <rollback plan>
- Today’s handoff: leaving notes for Sam at 11:00. Add 'revert routing if queue < 900 for 10m' in the handoff.

Broken / TODO items for later:
- Add a guard in autoscaler to prefer dedicated pools when queue type == "embedding" AND job priority == "low-cost" (reminder to open a PR against autoscaler).
- Finish writing the small python utility to parse nvlink logs into a summary CSV (start branch nvlink-parser).

Quick snips & commands (copyable):
- queue check: /opt/ops/tools/queue-stats --pool=batch-embeds --json | jq '.backlog'
- reroute (dry-run): ./route-override --from=batch-embeds --to=d-spot-3 --duration=30m --dry-run
- rsync logs: rsync -avz /tmp/dmesg-gnode-17.log debug@debug-bucket:/incoming/gnode-17/

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Can we carve a temporary 4xA100 slice in d-spot-3 for the next 48h to keep p95s stable? Who signs off on short-term capacity? (ping @platform-scheduling)
- Is the eu-west collector rollout yesterday related to the egress spike? Need eng-observability to correlate deploy times.

Notes to self:
- Keep the morning calls short; triage only the things that affect p95 or cause service errors.
- After stabilising queues, draft a quick postmortem note if we used temporary routing that includes cost delta and customer-facing impact (if any).

Handoff checklist for 11:00:
- Leave queue numbers + snapshot (attach output of /opt/ops/tools/queue-stats)
- Document any routing overrides done (CLI history + rollback steps)
- Attach logs (nvlink, dmesg) uploaded to debug bucket and note path

End of scratchpad. Will update inline as I run checks.
